newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end below 20,000,upside fades.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end below 20,000,upside fades.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished below the key 20,000 points level on Friday as the yen's strength and growing fears of an interest rate hike in Japan dulled the recent lustre of Tokyo stocks.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract lost 265 points to end at 19,840 after hitting a low of 19,780.

"The market has taken out the strong support for the medium term at 19,850 and failed to crack the resistance. That shows it's still very vulnerable," said a trader with a local institution who follows technical charts.
"The stronger yen just aggravated the whole thing. I think we should hover between 19,500 and 20,000 for now," he added.
He said the June Nikkei would need to close above 20,100 to resume its uptrend and that could take another week or more, in the absence of any good news.

A report in a Japanese financial daily speculating that the Bank of Japan could hike rates as early as July also dampened the market, while causing a sharp drop in Euroyen and Japanese government bond futures, dealers said.

Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Thursday night speech drew mixed reactions, with some traders viewing his words as a warning about further U.S. rate hikes while others saw him as signalling steady rates for now.
Greenspan said he expected economic growth to slow later this year and next, but added that the central bank would need to act if that did not prove to be the case.
The May MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 337.8 against its opening 341.5 on volume of 1,014 lots.
